meta.title: Decision-Prerequisite Questions Register
meta.principle: A decision is reasonably decidable only when every question it depends on is answered or consciously waived. Each row states what we HAVE (with official source links), what is MISSING, which decision it blocks, and a discovery suggestion (S-ids point to suggestions.html). Unknown values are never filled in.

statusLegend.answered: Answered from an official source this session.
statusLegend.partial: Partly answered; a defined gap remains.
statusLegend.open: Not answerable from currently verified sources.
statusLegend.decision: Needs an owner decision (default proposed and labelled).

questions.question: What is the minimum verified data needed to originate an NFL line?
questions.have: Official 2026 results (nfl.com by-week pages), standings PF/PA (nfl.com/standings), Week 10 injury report (nfl.com/injuries), club depth charts (club sites), full schedule (data/upstream/nfl-2026.json, NFL.com).
questions.missing: Play-by-play efficiency (EPA/play, success rate) is not published as an official league table; market closing lines are not available from an official source.
questions.blocks: How sharp any originated line can be (R5).
questions.discovery: S6 (official gamebooks/play-by-play), S4 (market snapshots).

questions.question: Do we have official game-by-game results for rating computation?
questions.have: Yes — nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-N pages list every final score with a per-game official URL (weeks 1-10 fetched 2026-11-13).
questions.missing: Nothing for results; margins are all that a rating needs.
questions.blocks: SRS-style ratings, empirical home-field, calibration backtests.
questions.discovery: None needed.

questions.question: Which team efficiency stats can be verified from official sources?
questions.have: NFL.com game pages publish points per game, yards per game, time of possession, sacks, INTs, turnover differential with league ranks (verified on steelers-at-bengals-2026-reg-10).
questions.missing: EPA/play, success rate, pace — no official league table found; do not infer them.
questions.discovery: S6 — parse official gamebooks (nfl.com) for play-level data or accept aggregate-only v0.

questions.question: Can a market line be verified from an official/official-partner source for comparison?
questions.have: ESPN (NFL official partner; ESPN BET) exposes week-10 odds on espn.com/nfl/odds — extraction attempted 2026-11-13 (see market-odds file).
questions.missing: Sportsbook operator pages (DraftKings/FanDuel/etc.) were not reachable for verification in this session; if ESPN extraction yields no spread/total/ML values, all market cells stay blank and flagged.
questions.blocks: Edge computation, CLV validation gate (R8), correlation estimation.
questions.discovery: S4 — schedule an odds-snapshot job at open/close each week.

questions.question: Can player prop markets be verified from any official source?
questions.have: Nothing verified. Books do not publish on official league domains.
questions.missing: All prop market data (lines, limits, hold).
questions.blocks: Player-prop combo strategies (R7) cannot be graded against a market; prop combos can only be graded on raw outcomes with modelled baselines.
questions.discovery: S4 (odds snapshots including props), or accept model-only prop lines with explicit caveat.

questions.question: When are official injury designations published, and what do the columns mean?
questions.have: NFL policy: practice reports Wed/Thu/Fri, game designations (Out/Doubtful/Questionable) after Friday practice, inactives 90 minutes before kickoff — operations.nfl.com is the official rulebook source; the nfl.com/injuries page shows Practice Status and Game Status columns.
questions.missing: Saturday inactives for week 10 are not yet published as of 2026-11-13 retrieval.
questions.blocks: Final deficiency grading (R11) — tracker must be re-run on game days.
questions.discovery: S7 — automate inactives ingestion 90 min pre-kickoff.

questions.question: Are club depth charts official, and what does the string column mean?
questions.have: Each club publishes a depth chart on its official site; the Lions page labels it '2026 Unofficial Depth Chart Compiled by Lions Football Communications' — club-official publication, explicitly unofficial in NFL terms. Columns are 1st-4th string.
questions.missing: Nothing structural; but depth charts are not updated on a fixed cadence and may lag roster moves.
questions.blocks: Whether a '2nd string replacement' claim is safe to make (R11) — we publish the club's own label alongside.
questions.discovery: S13 — week-to-week depth-chart drift monitor.

questions.question: What happens when an injured player does not appear on the published depth chart?
questions.have: Observed case: DET S Kerby Joseph (Game Status: Out) is not on the Lions' published depth chart (2026-11-13).
questions.missing: The club's intended replacement alignment.
questions.blocks: Replacement-string claim for that row — left blank + flagged (never infer).
questions.discovery: S13, plus official inactives + beat-writer-free official notes only (nfl.com news).

questions.question: How much sample is needed before a strategy result is skill rather than luck?
questions.have: Method defined: bootstrap confidence intervals + shrinkage toward the mean + closing-line-value check; variance of a 50/50 bet is 1.0 units² per unit stake.
questions.missing: Actual pick volume (competition not yet running).
questions.blocks: Leaderboard rewards (R7/R10) — gates defined but untested until N>=100 graded picks.
questions.discovery: S3 — pick ledger with pre-kickoff lock so volume accumulates.

questions.question: What are the correlation values between bet legs (parlays, prop combos)?
questions.have: Framework and estimator defined (strategies.html#correlation); same-game positive-correlation structure is well documented in industry literature but NOT verifiable from official league sources.
questions.missing: Empirical correlations require (a) our tracked picks and (b) market prices — both unavailable today.
questions.blocks: Parlay/prop-combo sizing rules (R9) — published values are labelled literature estimates and flagged.
questions.discovery: S5 — correlation job that runs once the pick ledger has >=50 same-game samples.

questions.question: What bankroll, unit size and reward budget govern the leaderboard?
questions.have: Nothing from the owner; a paper-unit default (1 unit = 1% of notional bankroll) is proposed.
questions.missing: Owner decision on real reward budget and eligibility.
questions.discovery: Owner decision — default adopted and labelled as a proposal in leaderboard.html.

questions.question: What staking rule removes overfitting and blow-up risk?
questions.have: Proposed: fractional Kelly (quarter-Kelly) capped at 3% of bankroll per pick, hard weekly exposure cap.
questions.missing: Owner risk tolerance.
questions.discovery: Owner decision — default labelled.

questions.question: Is the leaderboard graded weekly, season-long, or both?
questions.have: Proposed: weekly leaderboards + season-long table, both skill-adjusted.
questions.missing: Owner preference.
questions.discovery: Owner decision — both implemented.

questions.question: Do we track IR/designation/transaction moves that change depth charts?
questions.have: Official transactions exist at nfl.com/transactions and club sites; news items this week (e.g., 'Dolphins place QB Malik Willis on injured reserve') show the impact.
questions.missing: A fetched transactions feed (not ingested in this pass).
questions.discovery: S7 — extend the CI fetcher to nfl.com/transactions.

questions.question: How do weather and venue affect originated totals?
questions.have: Venue is in the official schedule (e.g., Paycor Stadium for PIT@CIN). Open-air vs dome is team knowledge — not published as an official data table.
questions.missing: Official forecast data at bet time; dome/open classification per stadium from an official source.
questions.discovery: S6 — gamebooks/official stadium pages; forecasts are non-official by nature and must be labelled.

questions.question: Which schedule-situational factors are derivable from official data?
questions.have: Rest days, travel, international games (Madrid W9), bye weeks (CHI/DEN/PHI/TB in W10), kickoff windows — all derivable from data/upstream/nfl-2026.json (NFL.com).
questions.missing: Nothing blocking; lookahead/look-ahead motivation is subjective and excluded.
questions.discovery: None needed.

questions.question: How can closing-line value be measured without a verified market source?
questions.have: Nothing verified yet; ESPN partner feed attempted (Q4).
questions.missing: Timestamped open/close market lines.

questions.question: How do strategy authors submit entries to the leaderboard?
questions.have: Proposed: a JSON file per strategy in data/nfl-analytics/submissions/ (or a GitHub issue), locked before kickoff.
questions.missing: Owner preference.
questions.discovery: Owner decision — repo-file protocol adopted as default.

questions.question: What player-usage data is verifiable (for prop baselines)?
questions.have: NFL.com player stat pages (targets, carries, yards) and game pages publish team leaders; official gamebooks list full participation.
questions.missing: Snap counts / route participation as an official table.
questions.discovery: S6 — parse official gamebooks.

questions.question: How often is verified data re-pulled and re-checked?
questions.have: This session: one verified snapshot dated 2026-11-13 (week 10). CI fetcher committed (scripts/fetch_nfl_analytics.py).
questions.missing: A cron schedule and post-game re-verification runs.
questions.discovery: S2 — add a scheduled workflow trigger (weekly + game-day).
